content:
Warner Bros. has announced it will test a new format with some iPhone users in the United States: HBO Max Shorts. Vertical video is already annoying enough, and the media giant adds that these clips are powered by artificial intelligence tools…

The company says AI is responsible for suggesting short-form content, with final decisions made by human editors.

"HBO Max Shorts" is designed to spotlight iconic and memorable scenes from the HBO Max library in a vertical, swipeable feed format, helping users discover content they want to watch […] The short-form clips are powered by an internally developed AI tool that uses machine learning algorithms and scene-level metadata to sift through thousands of hours of video, suggesting the most compelling and high-impact scenes for user exploration. After the AI tool makes suggestions, HBO Max editors decide which ones best showcase the stories audiences love, and the clips are then presented in a brand-new vertical video format to ensure smooth playback.

Reportedly, content will be personalised based on each user's viewing history; if a user is interested in a particular clip, they can start watching it immediately or add it straight from the feed to "My List".

Warner Bros. says it is currently testing the feature with a limited number of iPhone users in the US, but appears to have already decided to roll it out to other devices and markets later.

9to5Mac Opinion

Please, no. Warner Bros. breaking news: phones can also be held horizontally, not just vertically.
